[IMPORTANT:Results were written using a randomized dataset produced by Qualtrics to simulate what these sections will look like after data collection. These will be updated following the data collection.]
Gray et al. (2011) demonstrated that body focus induces redistribution of mind (as well as infers different moral statuses) instead of de-mentalization as suggested by theories of objectification. In a pre-registered experiment with an online Amazon Mechanical Turk American sample (N = 240), we replicated Experiments Four and Five of Gray et al. (2011).
decisions.reason: The dependent target identity (Gray, Knobe, Sheskin, Bloom, & Barrett, 2011, DOI 10.1037/a0025883, Experiments 4 and 5) and record type (replication) are confirmed in the source text. However, the supplied manuscript is a prospective Stage 1 registration report that explicitly states in the Abstract, Method, and Results sections that all reported statistical results were generated using a simulated randomized dataset from Qualtrics prior to actual data collection, and that the Discussion is only to be completed in Stage 2 following data collection. The shipped quote ('We successfully replicated all the findings') does not appear anywhere in the supplied text. Because simulated placeholder results are not actual empirical replication outcomes (as the blind coding also recognized via 'cannot_be_determined'), the replication outcome is undeterminable from the primary source.
